deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is German narrative history, written as lecture or reading notes, about the Wars of the Diadochi: the campaign between Eumenes of Cardia and Antigonus Monophthalmus in Upper Asia in 317–316 BC. The previous and next pages continue the same narrative. They cover Eumenes crossing the Euphrates and Tigris, his surrender by the Argyraspides, his execution, and the heading 'Dritter Zeitabschnitt' (third period, 315–301).

Content of the page, in order:
(1) Eumenes wins a battle (the battle of Paraitakene, 317 BC) but cannot exploit the victory because his army lacks discipline.
(2) Antigonus withdraws to Media; Eumenes winters (dated '316') in Persia, i.e. the Gabiene region.
(3) Two routes lead from Media to Susiana: the high road, and a route through the desert.
(4) Antigonus takes the desert route to surprise Eumenes and forbids camp fires despite the deep winter. The cold drives his troops to light fires anyway.
(5) Eumenes learns of this and uses a stratagem to delay Antigonus. In the sources this is lighting many fires on the hills to simulate a large encamped army; the notes only say 'eine Kriegslist'.
(6) The armies before the battle of Gabiene: Antigonus has 30000 men and 65 elephants; Eumenes has 40000 men and 114 elephants. The sentence continues on the next page.

There is no derivation, formula or computation to reconstruct. The hand and the content suggest notes from a history course rather than Gauss's own mathematical work. The bundle label 'HB.Lagrange1816' does not match the content.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.

Historical remark: the notes say the battle (Paraitakene, 317 BC) 'entschied sich für Eumenes'. Ancient sources (Diodorus XIX) treat it as essentially indecisive, with Eumenes having the slight advantage. This is a common simplification, not a slip.

Historical remark: the army totals are rounded. Diodorus gives Antigonus about 22000 infantry, 9000 cavalry and 65 elephants, and Eumenes about 36700 infantry, 6000 cavalry and 114 elephants. The elephant counts (65, 114) match the sources exactly; the man totals (30000, 40000) are approximations.

results.what: Narrative notes on the 317–316 BC campaign of Eumenes vs. Antigonus (Paraitakene, Antigonus's winter desert march, Eumenes's fire stratagem, forces at Gabiene)
results.modern_name: History of the Wars of the Diadochi (Second Diadoch War)
results.usually_credited_to: Ancient sources: Diodorus Siculus XIX, Plutarch's Life of Eumenes; standard 18th/19th-century ancient history textbooks

deep.surprise_reason: The page is non-mathematical school or lecture notes on ancient Greek history (the Diadochi), probably not even in Gauss's hand. It contains nothing of mathematical or historiographical novelty.
transcription_corrections: Line 'u. er fand ein[?] Kriegslist': the image reads 'eine Kriegslist'.
'65[?] Elephanten': the numeral is clearly 65. This agrees with Diodorus's figure for Antigonus's elephants at Gabiene, so the [?] can be removed.
'Antigonus er[?] kam': the word after 'Antigonus' is unclear in the image; it may be 'ankam' or 'nun kam'. Uncertain.
'um ihn so zu überfallen': the image may read 'u. ihn so zu überfallen'; the meaning is unchanged.
'Persien': the final letters are slightly ambiguous ('Persiens'/'Persienn'), but 'Persien' is the intended reading.
